segments.text: This is the biggest bet in history. One point four trillion dollars — from a single company.
Here's the problem. OpenAI has promised to spend one point four trillion dollars... on about thirteen billion a year in revenue.
And the deals are strange. Nvidia invests up to a hundred billion into OpenAI — which then spends it buying Nvidia's chips. The same money, going in a circle.
It's not just Nvidia. Broadcom, Oracle, Microsoft, AMD — over one point one trillion dollars in promises, all pointing back at one startup.
The strangest? AMD handed OpenAI the right to ten percent of its shares for a penny each — and OpenAI ordered ninety billion dollars of AMD chips. The customer now owns the supplier.
We've seen this before. In the dot-com bubble, chip makers funded their own buyers too. Then the Nasdaq fell seventy-eight percent.
One man is betting it all falls. Michael Burry — who called the two thousand eight crash — is shorting Nvidia with over a billion dollars.
But... Nvidia keeps beating every earnings call. The revenue is real, so far. Maybe it's not a bubble — maybe it's the biggest buildout ever.
Bubble? Or revolution? Nobody knows yet. Mr. WhyLab — we ask why.
